## Concepts

### RequestBoundary

**Purpose.** Let the outside world ask for things and receive answers, so each answer belongs to one pending call and unanswered calls remain unanswered.

**Principle.** A call arrives and becomes pending. When something answers, the reply travels back and a second answer is refused. If the caller times out or aborts first, waiting ends without recording an answer.

Actions:

- `request (…)`
- `respond (…)` — may refuse `NOT_PENDING`
- `register (…)`
- `cancel (…)`

### Assigning

**Purpose.** Let an author draft an assignment, publish it to everyone or selected sections,
and give each assignee a release with an optional individual due date.

**Principle.** Dana drafts a problem set for two sections and publishes it. Priya and Omar
each receive a release. Dana gives Omar a later due date, then clears that
override. Assigning the problem set to Omar again is refused because he already
has a release. After Dana archives the problem set, it can no longer be revised.

Actions:

- `createDraft (author, title, instructions, kind, availableAt, dueAt, closeAt, acceptsSubmissions, audience, targets, at)` — may refuse `ASSIGNMENT_AUDIENCE_INVALID`, `ASSIGNMENT_EVERYONE_NO_TARGETS`, `ASSIGNMENT_TARGETS_REQUIRED`
- `revise (assignment, title, instructions, kind, availableAt, dueAt, closeAt, acceptsSubmissions, audience, targets, at)` — may refuse `ASSIGNMENT_AUDIENCE_INVALID`, `ASSIGNMENT_EVERYONE_NO_TARGETS`, `ASSIGNMENT_TARGETS_REQUIRED`, `ASSIGNMENT_NOT_FOUND`, `ASSIGNMENT_NOT_REVISABLE`
- `publish (assignment, at)` — may refuse `ASSIGNMENT_NOT_FOUND`, `ASSIGNMENT_NOT_DRAFT`
- `archive (assignment, at)` — may refuse `ASSIGNMENT_NOT_FOUND`
- `assign (assignment, assignee, at)` — may refuse `ASSIGNMENT_NOT_FOUND`, `ASSIGNMENT_NOT_PUBLISHED`, `RELEASE_ALREADY_EXISTS`
- `setDueOverride (assignment, assignee, dueAt)` — may refuse `RELEASE_NOT_FOUND`
- `clearDueOverride (assignment, assignee)` — may refuse `RELEASE_NOT_FOUND`

Queries (standing questions the state answers):

- `_getDetail (assignment)` — promises at most one row
- `_getAssignments (…)` — promises any number of rows
- `_getAssigned (assignee)` — promises any number of rows
- `_getAssignees (assignment)` — promises any number of rows
- `_isAssigned (assignment, assignee)` — promises exactly one row
- `_getPublishedForAudience (audience)` — promises any number of rows
- `_getPublishedInWindow (start, end)` — promises any number of rows

### Authenticating

**Purpose.** Let a person create an account with a username and password, then use those
credentials to identify themselves later.

**Principle.** Nadia registers with the username nadia, a password, and her email address. A
user now exists for her. Later she authenticates with that username and
password and is recognized as the same user.

When Omar tries to register the username nadia, it is refused as taken. When
he tries to authenticate with a guessed password, he is turned away without
learning whether the username or the password was wrong.

Actions:

- `register (username, password, email)` — may refuse `INVALID_BODY`, `USERNAME_INVALID_LENGTH`, `USERNAME_INVALID_CHARS`, `PASSWORD_INVALID_LENGTH`, `USERNAME_TAKEN`
- `authenticate (username, password)` — may refuse `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`
- `changePassword (user, oldPassword, newPassword)` — may refuse `PASSWORD_INVALID_LENGTH`, `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`

Queries (standing questions the state answers):

- `_getById (user)` — promises at most one row
- `_getByUsername (username)` — promises at most one row
- `_getUserCount ()` — promises exactly one row
- `_search (query)` — promises any number of rows
- `_resolveIdentity (ref)` — promises exactly one row
- `_denotedUser (ref)` — promises at most one row

### Banking

**Purpose.** Give each learner a visible allowance of late days that staff can increase and
the learner can apply to individual items of work.

**Principle.** The course gives every learner three late days and limits each item to two. Ana
applies two days to an essay. She cannot apply two more to a problem set because
only one remains. Her advisor grants two extra days for conference travel, so
the second use succeeds. Ana later cancels that use. Its days return to her
balance, while the canceled use remains recorded.

Actions:

- `setTerms (allowance, perItemLimit, unitHours)`
- `grant (learner, days, reason, at)` — may refuse `LATE_DAYS_MUST_BE_POSITIVE`
- `apply (learner, item, days, at)` — may refuse `LATE_DAYS_MUST_BE_POSITIVE`, `LATE_DAYS_EXCEED_MAX`, `LATE_USE_ALREADY_EXISTS`, `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`
- `change (learner, item, days)` — may refuse `LATE_DAYS_EXCEED_MAX`, `LATE_DAYS_NEGATIVE`, `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, `LATE_USE_NOT_FOUND`
- `cancel (learner, item)` — may refuse `LATE_USE_NOT_FOUND`

Queries (standing questions the state answers):

- `_getTerms (…)` — promises exactly one row
- `_getBalance (learner)` — promises exactly one row
- `_getApplied (learner, item)` — promises at most one row
- `_getUses (learner)` — promises any number of rows
- `_getUsesForItem (item)` — promises any number of rows
- `_getGrants (learner)` — promises any number of rows

### Bookmarking

**Purpose.** Let a user keep a private list of items they want to return to later.

**Principle.** Ada saves a post, then saves another. Her list shows the newer bookmark first.
Saving the first post again is refused. Removing it succeeds once and is refused
the second time. Bob's bookmarks are independent of Ada's. Clearing an item
removes its bookmarks from every user's list and succeeds when none exist.

Actions:

- `save (user, item, at)` — may refuse `BOOKMARK_ALREADY_EXISTS`
- `unsave (user, item)` — may refuse `BOOKMARK_NOT_FOUND`
- `clearItem (item)`

Queries (standing questions the state answers):

- `_getSaved (user)` — promises any number of rows
- `_isSaved (user, item)` — promises exactly one row

### Categorizing

**Purpose.** Sort items into named categories. Each item belongs to at most one category, so
its home and each category's contents can be read directly.

**Principle.** Priya creates a Homework category and assigns a quiz to it. Assigning the quiz
to Exams moves it there. Unassigning it leaves it with no category, and a
second unassignment is refused. A second category named Homework is also
refused. Deleting Exams leaves every item in it uncategorized.

Actions:

- `createCategory (name, description)` — may refuse `CATEGORY_ALREADY_EXISTS`
- `assign (item, category)` — may refuse `CATEGORY_NOT_FOUND`
- `unassign (item)` — may refuse `ITEM_NOT_CATEGORIZED`
- `deleteCategory (category)` — may refuse `CATEGORY_NOT_FOUND`

Queries (standing questions the state answers):

- `_getCategory (item)` — promises at most one row
- `_getHome (item)` — promises at most one row
- `_getItems (category)` — promises any number of rows
- `_getAllCategories ()` — promises any number of rows

### Conversing

**Purpose.** Arrange items into conversations, with one root and replies that may have replies
of their own.

**Principle.** Noor starts a conversation with her question. Omar replies to it, and Priya
replies to Omar. An item can appear in only one conversation, so placing Omar's
answer again is refused. Omar's reply cannot be removed while Priya's reply is
beneath it. Removing the last node also removes the conversation.

Actions:

- `start (item, at)` — may refuse `ITEM_ALREADY_IN_CONVERSATION`
- `reply (item, parent, at)` — may refuse `ITEM_ALREADY_IN_CONVERSATION`, `PARENT_NODE_NOT_FOUND`
- `remove (node)` — may refuse `NODE_NOT_FOUND`, `NODE_HAS_CHILDREN`

Queries (standing questions the state answers):

- `_getThread (conversation)` — promises any number of rows
- `_getConversation (node)` — promises at most one row

- `_getItem (node)` — promises at most one row
- `_hasChildren (node)` — promises exactly one row
- `_getConversations ()` — promises any number of rows
- `_getConversationsByLastActivity ()` — promises any number of rows

### Flagging

**Purpose.** Let a person report a concern about a target and let a moderator resolve all
open concerns about that target as upheld or dismissed.

**Principle.** Sam reports a post as spam, and Rita reports the same post for another reason.
The post's open-flag count is now two. A moderator dismisses the reports, which
closes both flags. Sam cannot open another flag on the post while his first is
open. Unknown outcomes and targets without open flags are refused.

Actions:

- `flag (reporter, target, reason, at)` — may refuse `FLAG_ALREADY_EXISTS`
- `resolve (target, outcome)` — may refuse `VALIDATION_FAILED`, `FLAG_NOT_FOUND`
- `clearTarget (target)`

Queries (standing questions the state answers):

- `_getOpenTargets ()` — promises any number of rows
- `_getFlags (target)` — promises any number of rows

### Formatting

**Purpose.** Keep the rendered HTML for a target's source text and replace it when the source
changes.

**Principle.** Ben supplies a paragraph of source text and receives its rendered HTML. Editing
the source replaces that rendering. Clearing the target removes the rendering;
clearing it again still succeeds.

Actions:

- `setSource (target, source)`
- `clear (target)`

Queries (standing questions the state answers):

- `_getRendered (target)` — promises at most one row

### Grading

**Purpose.** Give each learner one grade per item, with a score, maximum, feedback, and a
clear draft, released, or excused status. Each grade keeps the maximum used
when it was recorded.

**Principle.** Ms. Okafor records Ana's essay grade as 42 out of 50, revises the draft to 45,
and releases it. Further recording is refused until she retracts it. She then
records 44 and releases every draft for the essay. Ben is excused, so recording
a score for him is refused. A score of 60 out of 50 is also refused.

Actions:

- `record (learner, item, evidence, grader, score, outOf, feedback, at)` — may refuse `SCORE_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `GRADE_ALREADY_RELEASED`, `LEARNER_EXCUSED`
- `scoreCriterion (learner, item, criterion, points, outOf, feedback)` — may refuse `SCORE_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `GRADE_ALREADY_RELEASED`, `LEARNER_EXCUSED`, `GRADE_NOT_FOUND`
- `release (learner, item, at)` — may refuse `GRADE_DRAFT_NOT_FOUND`
- `releaseItem (item, at)`
- `retract (learner, item, at)` — may refuse `GRADE_RELEASED_NOT_FOUND`
- `excuse (learner, item, grader, feedback, at)` — may refuse `GRADE_NOT_FOUND`
- `clearCriterionScores (criterion)`

Queries (standing questions the state answers):

- `_getGrade (learner, item)` — promises at most one row
- `_getGradesForLearner (learner)` — promises any number of rows
- `_getGradesForItem (item)` — promises any number of rows
- `_getCriterionScores (learner, item)` — promises any number of rows

### Itemizing

**Purpose.** Describe how an item is assessed with a label, a maximum score, and optional
ordered criteria.

**Principle.** Professor Lee configures the midterm as a grade item worth 100 points. She adds
Argument, worth 60, and Style, worth 40, in that order. A later `ensureItem`
request finds the existing item and leaves it unchanged. Adding a criterion to
an item that has not been configured is refused. Archiving the midterm removes
it from the active items.

Actions:

- `configureItem (item, label, maxPoints)` — may refuse `SCORE_OUT_OF_RANGE`
- `ensureItem (item, label, maxPoints)`
- `archiveItem (item)` — may refuse `GRADE_ITEM_NOT_FOUND`
- `addCriterion (item, name, maxPoints, position)` — may refuse `GRADE_ITEM_NOT_FOUND`
- `reviseCriterion (criterion, name, maxPoints, position)` — may refuse `CRITERION_NOT_FOUND`
- `removeCriterion (criterion)` — may refuse `CRITERION_NOT_FOUND`

Queries (standing questions the state answers):

- `_getItem (item)` — promises at most one row
- `_getItems ()` — promises any number of rows
- `_getCriteria (item)` — promises any number of rows
- `_getCriterion (criterion)` — promises at most one row

### Linking

**Purpose.** Record the ordered targets that a source links to, and support reading or
removing those links from either direction.

**Principle.** Noor's guide links to two worksheets, which are returned in the order she named
them. After she edits the guide to link to one worksheet, setting the links
replaces the previous list. Clearing a discarded worksheet's backlinks removes
it from every source. Clearing links that do not exist still succeeds.

Actions:

- `setLinks (source, targets)`
- `setLinksFrom (source, content)`
- `clearLinks (source)`
- `clearBacklinks (target)`

Queries (standing questions the state answers):

- `_getLinks (source)` — promises any number of rows
- `_getBacklinks (target)` — promises any number of rows

**Purpose.** Record when a target is locked and allow that lock to be removed later.

**Principle.** When the deadline passes, Dana locks a report and the action records the time.

### Notifying

**Purpose.** Give each person an inbox of events that concern them, with actions to mark,
dismiss, or clear notifications.

**Principle.** Someone replies to Mara's post, creating an unread notification that identifies
the event and its subject. Mara marks it read, which lowers her unread count
without removing it. She later marks every notification read and dismisses one.
Dismissing it again is refused. Noah cannot read or dismiss Mara's
notifications.

Actions:

- `notify (recipient, kind, subject, link, at)`
- `markRead (notification, recipient)` — may refuse `NOTIFICATION_NOT_FOUND`

- `dismiss (notification, recipient)` — may refuse `NOTIFICATION_NOT_FOUND`

Queries (standing questions the state answers):

- `_getUnreadCount (recipient)` — promises exactly one row

### Noting

**Purpose.** Let staff keep notes about a learner, choose whether to show each note to that
learner, and move notes through open, resolved, and archived states.

**Principle.** Ms. Okafor writes a note about Ana's project work, shows it to Ana, and Ana
acknowledges it. A second note about a missed meeting remains staff-only and has
a follow-up date. After the meeting, Ms. Okafor revises, resolves, and archives
that note. Revising a resolved note is refused; restoring it makes it open
again. Hiding an acknowledged note does not erase Ana's acknowledgment.

Actions:

- `write (author, learner, body, visibility, tags, followUpAt, at)` — may refuse `INVALID_VISIBILITY`
- `revise (note, body, visibility, tags, followUpAt, at)` — may refuse `INVALID_VISIBILITY`, `NOTE_NOT_FOUND`, `NOTE_NOT_OPEN`
- `resolve (note, at)` — may refuse `NOTE_NOT_FOUND`, `NOTE_NOT_OPEN`
- `archive (note, at)` — may refuse `NOTE_NOT_FOUND`, `NOTE_NOT_RESOLVED`
- `restore (note, at)` — may refuse `NOTE_NOT_FOUND`, `NOTE_NOT_RESTORABLE`
- `acknowledge (note, learner, at)` — may refuse `NOTE_NOT_FOUND`, `NOTE_NOT_LEARNER_VISIBLE`, `NOTE_NOT_OWNER`

Queries (standing questions the state answers):

- `_getNote (note)` — promises at most one row
- `_getActiveNotesFor (learner)` — promises any number of rows
- `_getShownTo (learner)` — promises any number of rows
- `_getByAuthor (author)` — promises any number of rows
- `_getOpenFollowUpsBefore (before)` — promises any number of rows

### Pinning

**Purpose.** Let a scope keep selected items above its ordinary listing, ordered by priority.

**Principle.** An administrator pins an announcement in a discussion. A second item with a
higher priority appears first, and changing a priority changes the order.
Pinning the same item twice in one scope is refused. Unpinning it succeeds once;
unpinning it again or changing the priority of an unpinned item is refused. The
same item may be pinned independently in another scope. Clearing an item
removes all of its pins and succeeds when none exist.

Actions:

- `pin (item, scope, priority, at)` — may refuse `ITEM_ALREADY_PINNED`
- `unpin (item, scope)` — may refuse `ITEM_NOT_PINNED`
- `setPriority (item, scope, priority)` — may refuse `ITEM_NOT_PINNED`
- `clearItem (item)`

Queries (standing questions the state answers):

- `_getPinned (scope)` — promises any number of rows
- `_isPinned (item, scope)` — promises exactly one row

### Profiling

**Purpose.** Keep a display name, bio, avatar, and contact email for each user, so the user

**Principle.** Priya's profile is created with her display name and email; her bio and avatar

### Reacting

**Purpose.** Let a person add or remove a named response, such as a thumbs-up or heart, on a

**Principle.** Noah reacts to a post with "up." Mara adds her own "up" and a "heart." Each
person may add one reaction of each kind to the target. Noah's second "up" is
refused. Removing it succeeds once and is refused the second time. Clearing a

### Resolving

**Purpose.** Mark at most one accepted answer for a question, including who accepted it and

**Principle.** Lena accepts Bo's answer to her question. When she later accepts another

is refused when the question has no resolution.

Actions:

- `accept (question, answer, by, at)`

- `_getTags (target)` — promises any number of rows
- `_getTargets (tag)` — promises any number of rows
- `_getByName (name)` — promises at most one row
- `_getAllTags ()` — promises any number of rows

### Timing

**Purpose.** Tell a caller the current moment, so a choice that needs a timestamp does not
invent one.

**Principle.** Noor asks what time it is and learns that it is 10:30. When she asks later, she
learns the later moment rather than the earlier answer.

Actions:

- `capture ()`

Queries (standing questions the state answers):

- `_now (…)` — promises exactly one row

### Tracking

**Purpose.** Record which items belong to each scope and which items each user has seen.

**Principle.** Dana registers a discussion in the Algebra course. It is unread for Bob until
he marks it seen. Marking it seen again or marking an unregistered item is
refused. Marking the whole scope seen records every remaining item and succeeds
when none remain. Unregistering the discussion removes it and all of its seen
marks; unregistering it again succeeds. Registering it twice is refused.

Actions:

- `register (item, scope)` — may refuse `ITEM_ALREADY_REGISTERED`
- `unregister (item)`
- `markSeen (user, item)` — may refuse `ITEM_NOT_REGISTERED`, `ITEM_ALREADY_SEEN`
- `markAllSeen (user, scope)`

Queries (standing questions the state answers):

- `_inScope (scope)` — promises any number of rows
- `_getUnread (user, scope)` — promises any number of rows
- `_getUnreadCount (user, scope)` — promises exactly one row

### Trashing

**Purpose.** Let an item be moved to trash, restored, or removed permanently.

**Principle.** Maya trashes a draft, recording who did it and when. She restores it, trashes
it again, and then purges it. Restoring or purging an item outside the trash is
refused, as is trashing an item already there.

Actions:

- `trash (item, by, at)` — may refuse `ITEM_ALREADY_TRASHED`
- `restore (item)` — may refuse `ITEM_NOT_TRASHED`
- `purge (item)` — may refuse `ITEM_NOT_TRASHED`

Queries (standing questions the state answers):

- `_isTrashed (item)` — promises exactly one row
- `_getTrashed ()` — promises any number of rows

```former
    createdAt
    editedAt
```

```former
Form the home feed by activity () as follows:
  each Conversing._getConversationsByLastActivity () has (conversation, root, item, createdAt)
    where item is intact
    where Locking._isLocked (target: conversation) has (locked)
    where Resolving._isResolved (question: item) has (resolved)
    where whether Categorizing._getHome (item) has (home)
    form a record of
      conversation
      root
      item
      createdAt
      category: home
      tags: each Tagging._getTags (target: item) has (tag, name: tagName)
        form a record of
          tag
          name: tagName
      locked
      resolved
      post: the post summary of (item)
      … the thread stats of (conversation)
```

```former
Form the home feed by creation () as follows:
  each Conversing._getConversations () has (conversation, root, item, createdAt)
    where item is intact
    where Locking._isLocked (target: conversation) has (locked)
    where Resolving._isResolved (question: item) has (resolved)
    where whether Categorizing._getHome (item) has (home)
    form a record of
      conversation
      root
      item
      createdAt
      category: home
      tags: each Tagging._getTags (target: item) has (tag, name: tagName)
        form a record of
          tag
          name: tagName
      locked
      resolved
      post: the post summary of (item)
      … the thread stats of (conversation)
```

```former
Form the unread of (user) in (scope) as follows:
  each Tracking._getUnread (user, scope) has (item)
    form a record of
      item
```

```former
Form the moderation queue () as follows:
  each Flagging._getOpenTargets () has (target, count)
    where Posting._getPost (post: target) has (author, content, createdAt, editedAt)
    where Formatting._getRendered (target) has (rendered)
    where whether Conversing._getNodeByItem (item: target) has (node)
    where whether Conversing._getConversation (node) has (conversation)
    form a record of
      target
      count
      conversation
      post: a record of
        author
        content
        createdAt
        editedAt
      rendered
      flags: each Flagging._getFlags (target) has (flag, reporter, reason, status, createdAt: flaggedAt)
        where Flagging._getFlags (target) has (flag, status: "open")
        form a record of
          flag
          reporter
          reason
          createdAt: flaggedAt
```

```former
Form the user page of (user) as follows:
  a record of
    profile: whether the profile face of (user)
    roles: each Roling._getRoles (user, context: "forum") has (role)
      where Roling._getRoleDetail (role) has (name)
      form a record of
        role
        name
    posts: each Posting._getByAuthor (author: user) has (post)
      where post is intact
      where whether Conversing._getNodeByItem (item: post) has (node)
      where whether Conversing._getConversation (node) has (conversation)
      form a record of
        item: post
        conversation
        post: whether the post summary of (item: post)
```

```former
Form the reaction counts on (target) as follows:
  each Reacting._countByKind (target) has (kind, count)
    form a record of
      kind
      count
```

```former
Form the bookmarked posts of (user) as follows:
  each the readable bookmarks of user has (item, savedAt)
    form a record of
      item
      savedAt
      post: the post summary of (item)
```

```former
Form the watched threads of (user) as follows:
  each Subscribing._getSubscriptions (user) has (target, subscribedAt)
    where target is readable
    where Conversing._getThread (conversation: target) has (node: rootNode, item: rootItem)
    where no Conversing._parentOf (node: rootNode)
    form a record of
      conversation: target
      subscribedAt
      post: whether the post summary of (item: rootItem)
      … the thread stats of (conversation: target), with blank leaves if absent
```

```former
Form the gradebook () as follows:
  a record of
    items: each Itemizing._getItems () has (item, label, maxPoints)
      form a record of
        item
        label
        maxPoints
    learners: each Rostering._getActiveStudents () has (user, section, rosterName, email)
      arranged by rosterName
      form a record of
        learner: user
        rosterName
        email
        section
        cells: each Itemizing._getItems () has (item: cellItem)
          where whether Grading._getGrade (learner: user, item: cellItem) has (grade, score, status)
          form a record of
            item: cellItem
            grade
            score
            status
```

### notifications.ReplyMentionsNotify

```reaction
when Conversing.reply (item, parent, at)
where
  the other users mentioned in item has (user: mentioned)
  Conversing._getItem (node: parent) has (item: parentItem)
  Posting._getPost (post: parentItem) and not (author: mentioned)
then
  request Notifying.notify (recipient: mentioned, kind: "mention", subject: item, link: item, at)
```

### notifications.ReplyNotifiesParentAuthor

```reaction
when Conversing.reply (item, parent, at)
where
  Conversing._getItem (node: parent) has (item: parentItem)
  Posting._getPost (post: parentItem) has (author: parentAuthor)
  Posting._getPost (post: item) and not (author: parentAuthor)
then
  request Notifying.notify (recipient: parentAuthor, kind: "reply", subject: item, link: item, at)
```

### notifications.ReplyNotifiesWatchers

```reaction
when Conversing.reply (item, parent, at)
where
  Conversing._getConversation (node: parent) has (conversation)
  Subscribing._getSubscribers (target: conversation) has (user: subscriber)
  Posting._getPost (post: item) and not (author: subscriber)
  Conversing._getItem (node: parent) has (item: parentItem)
  Posting._getPost (post: parentItem) and not (author: subscriber)
  subscriber is not mentioned in item
then
  request Notifying.notify (recipient: subscriber, kind: "followed_reply", subject: item, link: item, at)
```

## Endpoint input contracts

Before recording an action ask, the boundary rejects a body that is not an
object or lacks a required key. The response uses `INVALID_INPUT` and names
the path or missing key. A declared default fills an absent key. Endpoints
not listed here have no explicit input contract.

- `/assignments/archive` — requires `assignment`, `session`
- `/assignments/clear-due-override` — requires `assignee`, `assignment`, `session`
- `/assignments/create-draft` — requires `session`, `title`, `instructions`, `kind`, `availableAt`, `dueAt`, `acceptsSubmissions`, `audience`; fills `closeAt` with null when absent; fills `targets` with [] when absent
- `/assignments/for-me` — requires `session`
- `/assignments/get` — requires `assignment`
- `/assignments/publish` — requires `assignment`, `session`
- `/assignments/revise` — requires `session`, `assignment`, `title`, `instructions`, `kind`, `availableAt`, `dueAt`, `acceptsSubmissions`, `audience`; fills `closeAt` with null when absent; fills `targets` with [] when absent
- `/assignments/set-due-override` — requires `assignee`, `assignment`, `dueAt`, `session`
- `/assignments/staff-list` — requires `session`

- `/assignments/submit` — requires `assignment`, `content`, `session`
